# Pacific Hake J-SCOPE SDMs: Spatial Distribution and Biomass Forecasting

This repository contains the data, modeling pipelines, and simulation routines for analyzing transboundary spatial distribution and biomass shifts of Pacific hake (*Merluccius productus*) using J-SCOPE dynamic oceanographic forecasts.

**Associated Publication:**  
Marshall et al., *"Forecasting Pacific hake biomass distributions using ocean temperature reveals novel cross-shelf but weak latitudinal effects."* *PLOS Climate*.

## Repository Structure

├── data/
│   ├── _bath_200_utm_df       # 200 m isobath spatial vector for shelf break reference
│   ├── _namerica_state_utm_df # North American coastline basemap layer
│   ├── border_chull           # Spatial polygon bounding the U.S.–Canada EEZ domains
│   ├── hake_js                # Survey hauls matched to J-SCOPE temperature anomalies
│   └── temp_js                # Downscaled J-SCOPE temperature anomaly forecast grids
├── gam/                       # Model formulas, penalty structures, and candidate specifications
├── scripts/
│   ├── functions.R            # Custom delta-GLMM functions and posterior draw routines
│   ├── load.R                 # Asset loading and coordinate reference system transformations
│   ├── make_model_formulas.R  # Candidate GAM formulas across cohorts (Total, Age 2, Age 3–4, Age 5+)
│   ├── model_selection.R      # Leave-Future-Out cross-validation (LFO-CV) routines
│   ├── generate_output.R      # 5,000 Monte Carlo draws, regional aggregations, and 2024 forecasts
│   └── publish.R              # Publication figure scripts (Figures 1–6, Supplementary Figures)
├── outputs/
│   ├── model_performance/     # LFO-CV AUC and RMSE diagnostic summaries
│   ├── output_stats/          # Regional biomass summaries and key manuscript findings
│   └── figures/               # Final publication-ready TIFF graphics
├── run_hake_model_pipeline.R  # Master orchestration script
└── README.md


Analyses were performed in R (version 4.3+). Install required dependencies:

```r
pkgs <- c(
  "dplyr", "reshape2",
  "mgcv", "MASS", "pROC",
  "sf", "terra", "geosphere", "sgeostat",
  "ggplot2", "viridis", "patchwork", "gt",
  "ragg", "chromote", "webshot2", "here"
)

install.packages(setdiff(pkgs, rownames(installed.packages())))
```


2. Execution
Run the entire analytical pipeline end-to-end via the master orchestration script:

```
source("run_hake_model_pipeline.R")
```
The master script executes the modules sequentially:

Module 1 (load.R, functions.R): Loads hake survey data, regional boundary masks, and modeled temperature anomalies.

Module 2 (make_model_formulas.R): Sets up candidate occurrence and positive-density GAM structures across cohorts (Total, Age 2, Age 3–4, Age 5+).

Module 3 (model_selection.R): Conducts Leave-Future-Out cross-validation (LFO-CV) to identify optimal models.

Module 4 (generate_output.R): Generates 5,000 posterior Monte Carlo draws to produce regional summed biomass estimates and 2024 forecasts.

Module 5 (publish.R): Exports publication-ready figures.
